title: The Return of the Cattle

image.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bequest of Lucy Work Hewitt, 1934
image.license: Public domain. Released under Creative Commons Zero (CC0) through the Met's Open Access program

altText: A countryside farm scene in which cows are brought home by a group of people, including men, women and boys, in a soft rural landscape.

source.verifiedBy: Met Collection API object record: title, artist, date, medium, public-domain flag, credit line, tags (Farms, Boys, Men, Women, Cows) and image URLs read from the record

context: An oil painting by the French artist Hubert Robert, made around 1773–75. Robert is best known for views of ruins and gardens, so a farm scene with cows shows a different side of his work. The record's tags list cows, farms, and several people.

descriptions.k: Cows are coming home to the farm. Men, women, and boys walk with them. Can you find a cow? Which person do you think is leading the way? What sounds would you hear?
descriptions.g12: Hubert Robert, a French painter, shows the end of a day on a farm. Cows are coming home, and men, women, and boys are with them. The scene feels busy but friendly. What jobs do you think each person has? What sounds and smells are in this picture?
descriptions.g35: Hubert Robert is often known for paintings of old ruins, but here he painted a farm. Cows are being brought home by a group of people, including boys, men, and women. Look for how the animals and people are arranged, and how the scenery around them looks. Why might a painter choose an everyday farm moment instead of a grand event?
descriptions.g68: Painted around 1773–75, this scene shows the return of cattle to a farm. Hubert Robert, known for ruins and gardens, turns here to rural life, grouping animals and people across the canvas. Notice how the cows and figures create a rhythm of shapes and how soft light and trees set the mood. Eighteenth-century French viewers often liked idealized country scenes. Is this a realistic farm, an ideal one, or a mix?
descriptions.g910: Hubert Robert, famous for ruins and park views, here paints an evening scene of cattle returning home. Rural labor appears gentle and orderly: animals and figures are grouped to guide the eye, and soft light unifies the landscape. Many eighteenth-century paintings of country life were made for city audiences and present an idealized version of work on the land. How does Robert's picture balance observation with a pleasing, composed vision?
descriptions.g1112: In this canvas of about 1773–75, Hubert Robert offers a pastoral subject, cattle and country people at the close of the working day, within a career otherwise associated with ruins and architectural fantasies. Like much rural imagery made for urban French patrons, it can be read as sympathetic observation, as nostalgic idealization, or as both. The composition's harmony and softened labor invite questions about whose view of the countryside it records and what it leaves out.

teacherNote.context: Hubert Robert was a French painter best known for ruins and garden views. This farm scene of about 1773–75 shows him working in a pastoral mode that appealed to city audiences.
directions: Have students draw a quick map of where people and animals stand and discuss what it shows about composition.
Ask groups to list what a farm worker might notice that a city painter might leave out.
Compare this farm with the harbor and ruin scenes by other artists in the archive to see how landscapes tell different stories.
